title: regional-safety-latch-and-delayed-circuit-unwind
author: Evan Li
description: Motivation: during a recent regional egress saturation incident we saw repeated circuit flips as failover and rejoin events raced with KV-drain and egress throttles. This PR introduces a lightweight "safety latch" that gates circuit transitions when cross-region egress or KV pressure is detected, plus a delayed circuit-unwind path that staggers reopen attempts to prevent global flapping. Scope: runtime changes to the circuit breaker state machine, a small orchestration hook to make rejoin attempts exponential with jitter, telemetry additions, unit/integration tests, docs and an ops playbook. Key behavioral changes: 1) Safety latch: when a region experiences sustained egress saturation (configurable threshold) we mark the region as "latched" and disable automatic immediate reopen for tenant circuits that were tripped due to remote egress failures. Latched state can be observed via telemetry and toggled by ops. 2) Delayed unwind: instead of immediate circuit re-open attempts after cooldown, reopens are windowed and backoff-ed per-tenant cohort; the earliest reopen path only allows a small percentage of requests (10%) for validation probes. 3) KV-drain coordination: we add a transient hold state during KV draining so in-flight requests do not trigger reopen noise. 4) Soft rollback: a runtime flag (safety_latch.enabled=false) allows rollback without restart. Commits: - add safety latch state machine and guards (runtime/circuit_breaker/latch.go) - make reopen scheduler pluggable and add delayed-unwind implementation (runtime/circuit_breaker/unwind_scheduler.go) - KV drain hold-state integration and tests (runtime/kv/kv_drain_hold.go, runtime/kv/kv_drain_hold_test.go) - telemetry: new metrics and labels (telemetry/metrics/safety_latch_metrics.yaml) - docs and ops runbook (docs/ops/safety-latch.md, ops/deploy/hotfix-rollback.md) Testing: unit tests for state transitions (100% coverage on new state machine), integration test simulating cross-region egress stress (integration_tests/slo_regression.yml). CI: initial run showed one flaky integration test (inflight preservation under extreme backpressure) which was addressed by increasing a test time window and re-recording golden traces; final CI passed. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag, start with Canary region in us-west-2 for 24h, monitor slo_regional_reopen_rate and slo_error_budget_burn metrics, then increment to 25% of regions before global. Ops/rollback: runtime flag for immediate disable, runbook added describing steps to un-latch a region and force reopen for urgent recovery. Related work: follows on ENG-4207 (regional failover jitter work) and complements ENG-4310 (kv-coordination fixes). Merge notes: squash-merged after approvals and green CI. This PR was driven as a precautionary hotfix to reduce incident recurrence and to provide better observability for coordination between egress, kv-drain, and circuit state transitions.

reviews: Aisha Kapoor: High-level LGTM. Please add an observability note about the new metric cardinality. Asked to ensure the telemetry labels are low-cardinality. (ACTION: addressed in telemetry commit).

Miguel Santos: Requested change: make the latch TTL configurable per-region and add unit tests for TTL expiry. Also asked for explicit gating so tenant-specific reopen percent can be changed at runtime. (ACTION: added region TTL config and test coverage in latch_test.go).

Riya Patel: Noted a potential race between kv-drain hold and scheduled reopen; suggested adding a small reconciliation loop that re-checks kv state before allowing probe requests. Evan replied that a lightweight reconciler was added to unwind_scheduler.go and included tests. Approved after CI green.
release_notes: Introduce regional safety latch to prevent mass reopen flapping during egress/KV pressure, and delayed circuit-unwind to stagger reopen attempts. Configurable per-region TTL and runtime flag for rapid rollback. Improves SLO stability during failover events.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: new state machine could delay legitimate reopen for some tenants and increase latency for recovery. Mitigations: feature-flagged rollout, canary in us-west-2, runtime toggle to disable latch, observability hooks (slo_reopen_rate, safety_latch_state, kv_drain_hold_count) and a runbook for forced unlatching.
